title: Pay for musicians around 1910-1920
summary: Barnes says pay was a dollar and a half to three dollars early on, rising to four or five dollars after the First War.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah, I wish you would, sure. And I don't do it. But in the meantime, I should do it. It takes a dollar to chuck it. So I was going to ask about the pay for those things. Yeah. Yeah. How much did you get paid in the old days, around 1910 to 1920 period, say around the time of the First World War when you first started playing?

Well, I tell you, during the very, very first time, we had two and a half or maybe three dollars. Okay. Because we didn't get any money from music until the first one. That's when you started getting five dollars and that. But before, it was a dollar and a half, two and a half, maybe three dollars. You see? Well, after that, you started getting the four dollars, five dollars after the first first war. Yeah. But now you see, it's all together different now.
